+package pir
+
+import (
+	"encoding/binary"
+
+	"easypir/refwire"
+	"easypir/safeaes"
+)
+
+// knownCount is the number of superblocks (the first ones) for which the
+// client keeps, per hint, the parity of the hint restricted to that
+// superblock. Their keys never need to reach the server: ReduceRequest drops
+// them, and the response carries no key parity for them.
+const knownCount = 1
+
+func knownSBs(p refwire.Params) uint64 {
+	if p.SBNum < knownCount {
+		return p.SBNum
+	}
+	return knownCount
+}
+
+// requestLen is the length of a reduced request: the keys of the superblocks
+// knownSBs..SBNum-1, then the SBSize explicit offsets packed as in refwire.
+func requestLen(p refwire.Params) int {
+	return int(p.SBNum-knownSBs(p))*16 + (int(p.SBSize)*int(p.OffsetBits())+7)/8
+}
+
+// responseLen is the length of a response: one list candidate per
+// superblock, then the key parity of every superblock whose key was sent.
+func responseLen(p refwire.Params) int {
+	return int(2*p.SBNum-knownSBs(p)) * 16
+}
+
+// packOffsets writes width-bit offsets least-significant bit first into dst,
+// which must be zeroed and exactly (len(offsets)*width+7)/8 bytes long.
+func packOffsets(dst []byte, offsets []uint32, width uint) {
+	var acc uint64
+	var have uint
+	k := 0
+	for _, offset := range offsets {
+		acc |= uint64(offset) << have
+		have += width
+		for have >= 8 {
+			dst[k] = byte(acc)
+			k++
+			acc >>= 8
+			have -= 8
+		}
+	}
+	if have > 0 {
+		dst[k] = byte(acc)
+	}
+}
+
+// unpackOffsets is the inverse of packOffsets (width at most 32).
+func unpackOffsets(src []byte, offsets []uint32, width uint) {
+	var acc uint64
+	var have uint
+	k := 0
+	mask := uint64(1)<<width - 1
+	for i := range offsets {
+		for have < width {
+			acc |= uint64(src[k]) << have
+			k++
+			have += 8
+		}
+		offsets[i] = uint32(acc & mask)
+		acc >>= width
+		have -= width
+	}
+}
+
+// subKeyInto is refwire.SubKey without allocation: the 16-byte key of one tag
+// and superblock under the expanded master key.
+func subKeyInto(master *safeaes.RoundKeys, tag uint32, sb uint64, out *[16]byte) {
+	var src [16]byte
+	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(src[:8], uint64(tag)<<35+sb)
+	safeaes.MMO(master, out, &src)
+}
+
+// prfWord is util.PRFEvalWithLongKey on expanded round keys.
+func prfWord(rk *safeaes.RoundKeys, x uint64) uint64 {
+	var src, dst [16]byte
+	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(src[:8], x)
+	safeaes.MMO(rk, &dst, &src)
+	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(dst[:8])
+}
+
+// keyPRF is util.PRFEval: expand the key, then evaluate once.
+func keyPRF(key *[16]byte, x uint64) uint64 {
+	var rk safeaes.RoundKeys
+	safeaes.ExpandKey(key, &rk)
+	return prfWord(&rk, x)
+}
+
+// keyTables drive a table-based AES-128 key schedule that produces exactly
+// safeaes.ExpandKey's round keys. It runs on other execution units than the
+// AESKEYGENASSIST-based assembly, so interleaving the two is faster than
+// either alone.
+type keyTables struct {
+	t0, t1, t2, t3 [256]uint32
+}
+
+func newKeyTables() *keyTables {
+	var sbox [256]byte
+	p, q := byte(1), byte(1)
+	for {
+		if p&0x80 != 0 {
+			p = p ^ (p << 1) ^ 0x1b
+		} else {
+			p = p ^ (p << 1)
+		}
+		q ^= q << 1
+		q ^= q << 2
+		q ^= q << 4
+		if q&0x80 != 0 {
+			q ^= 0x09
+		}
+		x := q ^ (q<<1 | q>>7) ^ (q<<2 | q>>6) ^ (q<<3 | q>>5) ^ (q<<4 | q>>4)
+		sbox[p] = x ^ 0x63
+		if p == 1 {
+			break
+		}
+	}
+	sbox[0] = 0x63
+	tb := &keyTables{}
+	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
+		s := uint32(sbox[i])
+		tb.t0[i], tb.t1[i], tb.t2[i], tb.t3[i] = s, s<<8, s<<16, s<<24
+	}
+	return tb
+}
+
+// expand2 expands two keys at once (interleaved for instruction-level
+// parallelism).
+func (tb *keyTables) expand2(ka, kb *[16]byte, ra, rb *safeaes.RoundKeys) {
+	a0 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ka[0:])
+	a1 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ka[4:])
+	a2 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ka[8:])
+	a3 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ka[12:])
+	b0 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(kb[0:])
+	b1 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(kb[4:])
+	b2 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(kb[8:])
+	b3 := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(kb[12:])
+	ra[0], ra[1], ra[2], ra[3] = a0, a1, a2, a3
+	rb[0], rb[1], rb[2], rb[3] = b0, b1, b2, b3
+	rc := uint32(1)
+	for r := 4; r < 44; r += 4 {
+		ta := tb.t0[byte(a3>>8)] ^ tb.t1[byte(a3>>16)] ^ tb.t2[byte(a3>>24)] ^ tb.t3[byte(a3)] ^ rc
+		tv := tb.t0[byte(b3>>8)] ^ tb.t1[byte(b3>>16)] ^ tb.t2[byte(b3>>24)] ^ tb.t3[byte(b3)] ^ rc
+		a0 ^= ta
+		b0 ^= tv
+		a1 ^= a0
+		b1 ^= b0
+		a2 ^= a1
+		b2 ^= b1
+		a3 ^= a2
+		b3 ^= b2
+		ra[r], ra[r+1], ra[r+2], ra[r+3] = a0, a1, a2, a3
+		rb[r], rb[r+1], rb[r+2], rb[r+3] = b0, b1, b2, b3
+		rc <<= 1
+		if rc&0x100 != 0 {
+			rc ^= 0x11b
+		}
+	}
+}
